beats.label: S1 · Logan's stroke
beats.text: Logan collapses from a stroke at his birthday party, leaving Kendall as acting CEO — who immediately discovers the company carries $3 billion in hidden personal debt.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Sets the core premise: Kendall in charge without mandate, financial crisis forcing him to seek outside money — which opens the door to Sandy and Stewy.

beats.label: S1 · The Stewy trap
beats.text: Kendall brings in college friend Stewy to inject capital, but Greg spots Stewy meeting privately with Sandy Furness — Logan's rival — suggesting the rescue money is a Trojan horse.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Introduces Sandy and Stewy as recurring antagonists and plants the suspicion that will fuel Kendall's hostile-takeover gambit.

beats.label: S1 · No-confidence crushed
beats.text: Kendall assembles a board majority to oust Logan, but Logan storms the vote, bullies members back to his side, and fires everyone who voted against him — including Kendall and Frank.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Logan's dominance is re-established; Kendall is fired and humiliated, which drives him toward the more radical hostile-takeover route with Sandy and Stewy.

beats.label: S1 · Shiv's secret and Kendall's deal
beats.text: Shiv quietly joins Logan's political enemy Gil Eavis's campaign. At Tom's bachelor party, a fired and furious Kendall cuts a deal with Sandy and Stewy for a hostile takeover.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Both threads have long tails: Shiv's political alignment shapes her leverage in S2, and the Sandy/Stewy relationship resurfaces through S3.

beats.label: S1 · Doddy's death
beats.text: After the wedding-day takeover collapses, Kendall takes drugs with Doddy — a waiter Logan fired. Their car crashes into water; Doddy drowns and Kendall flees.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Logan now holds lethal leverage over Kendall, fundamentally reshaping the power dynamic between them for the rest of the series.

beats.label: S1 · Son turns on father
beats.text: Logan buries the Doddy case in exchange for Kendall taking public blame for the cruise scandal. At the press conference, Kendall instead names Logan as the man behind the cover-up.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kendall's defection is the inciting event for all of S2 — the family is now publicly at war, and Logan's enigmatic smile leaves his intentions completely opaque.

cliffhanger.text: Kendall has just accused his father of directing the cruise cover-up on live television — and Logan watched it happen with a smile. The war is now public, but Logan's next move is impossible to read.
questions: Does Logan's smile mean he respects Kendall for finally fighting back, or is he already planning his response?
What will happen to Greg, who stood beside Kendall at the press conference holding the incriminating cruise documents?
Can Kendall sustain a public war against his father — and what leverage does Logan still hold over him through Doddy?

characters.name: Logan Roy
characters.line: Waystar's patriarch CEO, back in full control after surviving a stroke and crushing Kendall's coup — and holding Doddy's death over his son.

characters.name: Kendall Roy
characters.line: Logan's second son, fired and then co-opted as scapegoat — who just publicly accused his father on live TV, holding nothing but his word.

characters.name: Shiv Roy
characters.line: Logan's daughter, secretly named his preferred successor, newly married to Tom, having quietly defected to a rival politician's campaign.

characters.name: Roman Roy
characters.line: Logan's youngest son, who sided with his father at the board vote and is beginning a management training program inside Waystar.

characters.name: Tom Wambsgans
characters.line: Shiv's new husband, appointed to head Parks and Cruises — and already sitting on secret knowledge of the cruise cover-up.

characters.name: Greg Hirsch
characters.line: Logan's great-nephew, a low-level Waystar employee who secretly kept copies of the cruise documents and just stood beside Kendall at the press conference.

characters.name: Gerri Kellman
characters.line: Waystar's general counsel, who covertly backed Kendall's failed coup but has survived in her role — her loyalty follows whoever holds power.

beats.label: S2 · The CEO promise
beats.text: Logan privately names Shiv as his chosen successor, pulling her away from Gil Eavis's campaign — but refuses to honor the promise publicly when it matters.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Shiv's belief that she is the chosen heir drives her decisions all season; Logan's pattern of private promises and public refusals is the engine of their relationship.

beats.label: S2 · Cruise scandal breaks public
beats.text: The Roys pursue Pierce Global Media, but a magazine exposé on the cruise cover-up goes online mid-negotiation, derailing the deal and forcing the family into Senate testimony.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The public exposure is the engine for the rest of S2 — hearings, a whistleblower, and eventually the need for a scapegoat all flow directly from here.

beats.label: S2 · Senate hearings
beats.text: Tom testifies disastrously. Shiv privately intimidates the whistleblower's key witness into silence. Every member of the family is now visibly implicated in the cover-up.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Tom's exposure deepens his prison-fear arc and seeds his eventual betrayal of Shiv; Shiv's witness tampering makes her as culpable as anyone.

beats.label: S2 · Rhea named CEO
beats.text: Logan installs outside executive Rhea Jarrell as his successor — a non-family buffer. She resigns the moment she grasps she is the designated scapegoat, not the real heir.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Rhea's appointment and swift exit prove Logan will sacrifice any ally rather than name a real successor, setting up the blood-sacrifice ultimatum.

beats.label: S2 · Blood sacrifice
beats.text: Logan tells his children that someone must fall publicly for the scandal. He privately settles on Kendall — the son he said is not a 'killer' — and arranges a press conference.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The season's central revelation: Logan sees Kendall as expendable. That judgment is what Kendall defies at the press conference.

beats.label: S2 · Kendall turns again
beats.text: At the press conference, Kendall abandons his script and names Logan as the man who personally oversaw the cruise cover-up. Greg stands beside him with the documents. Logan smiles.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Kendall's public defection — backed by Greg and the documents — launches the open father-son war that is the spine of S3.

cliffhanger.text: Kendall has accused Logan for the second time in two seasons, now in public with documentary evidence. Logan watched and smiled. The family is openly at war and the company is still under federal scrutiny.
questions: What does Logan's smile mean — does he respect Kendall for finally fighting back, or is he already one move ahead?
Can Kendall build a coalition inside Waystar strong enough to unseat his father from outside the building?
With Tom still exposed by the hearings and Shiv's CEO promise never honored, how long before the family splinters further?

characters.name: Logan Roy
characters.line: Still CEO, publicly accused by his own son for the second time — watching Kendall's rebellion on television with an opaque smile.

characters.name: Kendall Roy
characters.line: Outside the company, having just publicly accused his father on live TV — armed only with Greg and the cruise documents.

characters.name: Shiv Roy
characters.line: Inside Waystar as President of Domestic Operations, but Logan's private CEO promise was never honored and she knows it.

characters.name: Roman Roy
characters.line: Back inside the company after a hostage situation abroad; developing genuine instincts for the business and an unusual dependency on Gerri's approval.

characters.name: Tom Wambsgans
characters.line: Terrified of prison over his role in the cruise cover-up; his marriage to Shiv is visibly deteriorating.

characters.name: Greg Hirsch
characters.line: Stood beside Kendall at the press conference holding incriminating documents — now caught between two openly warring sides of the family.

characters.name: Gerri Kellman
characters.line: Waystar's general counsel, survived the Senate hearings; Roman is developing a strange reliance on her that she has begun to leverage.

beats.label: S3 · Siblings stay with Logan
beats.text: Kendall declares public war on Logan, but his siblings calculate no personal benefit in joining him and stay with their father. Gerri becomes interim CEO; Shiv gets a title with no real power.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the season's alignment: Kendall is alone and exposed, his siblings are inside but sidelined, and Logan retains control despite the public scandal.

beats.label: S3 · DOJ and the prison threat
beats.text: The DOJ opens a criminal probe into the cruise cover-up. Tom volunteers to go to prison to protect the family. Logan pressures the White House, and the investigation eventually settles quietly.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Tom's willingness to sacrifice himself is the seed of his later betrayal of Shiv — visible loyalty that Logan notices and eventually rewards.

beats.label: S3 · Shareholder standoff
beats.text: Sandy and Stewy threaten to strip the Roys of voting control. Logan is incapacitated; his children negotiate a fragile deal with Sandy's daughter Sandi — without his knowledge or approval.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The children acting without Logan signals they can organize without him, which sharpens his urgency to complete the GoJo deal and lock them out of succession.

beats.label: S3 · Matsson proposes a flip
beats.text: Roman back-channels GoJo CEO Matsson and discovers Matsson wants to acquire Waystar, not be acquired. Logan accepts — agreeing to sell the whole company without consulting his children.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The GoJo acquisition is the central conflict of both the S3 finale and all of S4 — this is the moment Logan decides to sell over his children's heads.

beats.label: S3 · Children find the veto
beats.text: The siblings discover Logan agreed to sell without them, ending any path to succession. They locate a clause in Logan and Caroline's divorce granting them veto power over a change of control.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The veto clause is the children's only remaining leverage — and its removal by Tom's tip-off is the decisive act of the finale.

beats.label: S3 · Tom's betrayal
beats.text: Shiv tells Tom about the planned revolt. Tom tips off Logan, who quietly renegotiates Caroline's agreement, stripping the children of their veto. They arrive at the confrontation with nothing.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Tom's betrayal is the season's central twist and shapes all of S4 — his allegiance to Logan over Shiv upends their marriage and repositions him inside the company.

cliffhanger.text: Logan has sold Waystar to GoJo over his children's heads, and the veto they found was neutralized by Tom's tip-off. The children are shut out of succession; Tom has thrown in with Logan; and the sale now looks unstoppable.
questions: Will the children find another way to block or reshape the GoJo sale before it closes?
What does Tom's betrayal of Shiv mean for their marriage — and what does Logan owe him in return?
Who, if anyone, emerges as Logan's real successor now that the company is being sold to an outsider?

characters.name: Logan Roy
characters.line: Has agreed to sell Waystar to GoJo, outmaneuvering his children with Tom's help and Caroline's compliance — the deal is his to finalize.

characters.name: Kendall Roy
characters.line: Exhausted and near-suicidal after his public rebellion failed; briefly reunited with his siblings against Logan — then outmaneuvered again.

characters.name: Shiv Roy
characters.line: Inside the company but sidelined; has just discovered Tom betrayed her to their father, stripping the children of their last leverage.

characters.name: Roman Roy
characters.line: Instrumental in opening the Matsson deal; pulled between his siblings and his father throughout, landing on Logan's side by default.

characters.name: Tom Wambsgans
characters.line: Has betrayed Shiv by tipping off Logan — closer to Logan's inner circle now, with his marriage likely over and his position newly cemented.

characters.name: Greg Hirsch
characters.line: Tom has cryptically offered him a chance at significant ascension inside the company — the terms and nature of the offer are still unclear.

characters.name: Lukas Matsson
characters.line: GoJo's CEO; has proposed acquiring Waystar and secured Logan's agreement — his completion of the deal is now the dominant threat to the Roy children.

beats.label: S4 · Siblings buy Pierce
beats.text: Kendall, Shiv, and Roman break from Logan and jointly outbid him for Pierce Global Media — their first coordinated win against their father, and proof they can operate as a unit.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Establishes the siblings' alliance and their capacity to act without Logan, which makes his sudden death all the more destabilizing for them.

beats.label: S4 · Logan dies
beats.text: Logan collapses on his plane to Sweden and dies before any succession plan is in place. The siblings receive his body at the airport and announce his death together.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The central event of the series — everything after is about what the children do in the vacuum Logan leaves, with no father to fight or appease.

beats.label: S4 · Co-CEO compromise
beats.text: A document in Logan's safe names Kendall his successor, but Roman holds the COO title — so the brothers split the role as co-CEOs and promise to include Shiv in decisions.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The co-CEO arrangement is inherently unstable and sets up the Norway confrontation where the brothers' inability to present a united front costs them the company.

beats.label: S4 · Norway: deal slips away
beats.text: The brothers try to kill the GoJo deal at Matsson's retreat, but Roman explodes and calls it off in person. Matsson bypasses them and offers Waystar's board $192 per share directly.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Roman's impulsive blowup removes the brothers' negotiating position, handing Matsson direct access to the board and sealing the acquisition's momentum.

beats.label: S4 · Election night
beats.text: Roman pressures ATN into prematurely calling Wisconsin for far-right candidate Mencken — betting that a Mencken presidency will produce an antitrust block of the GoJo deal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The Mencken gambit is the brothers' last real attempt to kill GoJo; that it immediately backfires is the condition that collapses Roman at the funeral.

beats.label: S4 · Matsson picks Tom
beats.text: Matsson reveals he wants Tom — not Shiv — as his American CEO, judging Tom more compliant. Greg tips off the siblings, briefly uniting them behind Kendall to block the deal.
beats.whyLoadBearing: Matsson's choice of Tom over Shiv is what temporarily realigns the siblings — and makes Shiv's defection at the final vote all the more consequential.

beats.label: S4 · Shiv's vote
beats.text: At the final board vote, Shiv defects — deciding she trusts Kendall with unchecked power less than she trusts the deal. Tom is named CEO. Roman walks away. Kendall loses everything.
beats.whyLoadBearing: The series' final reckoning: none of the children inherit, the company passes to an outsider, and the siblings' alliance collapses on the last possible vote.

cliffhanger.text: Waystar has been sold. Tom is CEO. Kendall has lost everything he spent four seasons fighting for. Roman has accepted defeat. Shiv is pregnant and returning to Tom's side — the Roy family's reign is over.
questions: Can Shiv and Tom rebuild their relationship after all the betrayals between them, with a child on the way?
What does Kendall do now — a man who has no company, no father, and no purpose left to organize his life around?
Is Roman's acceptance of defeat genuine peace, or has he simply run out of fight?

characters.name: Kendall Roy
characters.line: Lost the CEO chair at the final vote when Shiv defected — the company is sold and he has nothing left to fight for.

characters.name: Shiv Roy
characters.line: Voted against her own brother, returned to Tom's side, and is pregnant — having chosen the deal over loyalty to Kendall.

characters.name: Roman Roy
characters.line: Walked away from the final vote and accepted that neither he nor his siblings were ever fit to inherit their father's company.

characters.name: Tom Wambsgans
characters.line: Named CEO of the combined Waystar-GoJo entity by Matsson — elevated entirely through compliance and proximity to power, not capability.

characters.name: Logan Roy
characters.line: Dead — his sudden death without a succession plan in place is the premise of the entire season.

characters.name: Lukas Matsson
characters.line: GoJo's CEO, now the effective owner of Waystar, having installed Tom as his chosen American operator and closed the deal over the Roys' objections.

characters.name: Greg Hirsch
characters.line: Positioned as Tom's close aide in the new power structure — having traded loyalty for proximity to whoever currently holds power.
